source_row.stem: A client's folate level is significantly below normal, and a colleague assumes this deficiency would cause the opposite red blood cell change from a B12 deficiency. Similar to B12 deficiency, this can instead cause:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Microcytic anemia exclusively, a pattern more typically associated with iron deficiency than with this particular deficiency","B":"No effect on red blood cells at all, despite this nutrient's known role in DNA synthesis for developing cells","C":"Hypocalcemia, an electrolyte disturbance not typically caused by a deficiency of this particular nutrient","D":"Larger-than-normal red cells, since this nutrient is also essential for building new red cells correctly"}}
source_row.rationale: Folate deficiency, like B12 deficiency, impairs DNA synthesis in developing red blood cells, resulting in macrocytic anemia, though folate deficiency typically does not cause the neurological symptoms seen with B12 deficiency.
